lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: Use contact details a recruiter can reach if these are placeholders on the submitted résumé.
items.because: The phone number and website may be placeholders.

items.says: Clarify what “update speed” measures.
items.because: The result is hard to interpret without knowing whether it means download time, throughput, or completion time.

items.says: Explain how the 60% improvement was measured.
items.because: The measurement basis would make the result easier to interpret.

items.says: Clarify whether you built the rig’s hardware, software, or both.
items.because: The current wording does not establish the rig’s scope.

items.says: Clarify what “400 tests” counts.
items.because: It could refer to the rig’s scope or to a test-suite count.

items.says: Explain what evidence the logger captured and how it contributed to finding the causes.
items.because: The wording can sound as if the logger alone identified the root causes.

items.says: Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The sample rate is below the Nyquist requirement.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter `volatile` does not by itself fix the race condition.
items.because: `volatile` does not provide synchronization or atomicity.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the motor-controller rewrite.
Give the measurement basis and time period for the jitter and fault reductions, if available.
Resolve this result’s overlap with the Formula Student bullet before retaining both.
items.because: The same 300-unit motor-control result appears under that project.

items.says: Clarify what part of the test automation you personally implemented, if useful for the target role.
Specify the measurement period for the reduction in returns if it matters.
Clarify the relationship between the calibration procedure and the complaint reduction.
items.because: The current wording does not explain how the procedure relates to the count.

items.says: Provide the comparison period or explain how complaints were tracked, if verifiable.
items.because: That would make the complaint reduction clearer.

items.says: Clarify your design contribution if “designed” could be mistaken for a team-wide effort.
Replace or remove the promotional description.
items.because: “Next-generation” and “redefines” are broad claims that do not explain what you built.

items.says: Clarify the conditions under which average current was measured.
items.because: The reading or transmission schedule may affect comparability.

items.says: Verify that “built two stations” accurately describes what the school did.
Clarify your leadership scope if “Electronics Lead” does not make it clear.
Robot-fleet firmware appears not to belong under the Formula Student electric-car project.
items.because: It conflicts with the project context and resembles work described under Voltline.

items.says: State who wrote and tested the dashboard firmware and what you contributed.
items.because: The passive phrasing leaves ownership uncertain.

items.says: The 300-robot motor-control result appears duplicated or misattributed to the Formula Student project.
items.because: It repeats the Voltline achievement and conflicts with the project’s dates and context.

items.says: Reconsider how the Tools list groups its items.
items.because: It combines languages, a microcontroller platform, measurement equipment, and FPGA.

items.says: Support FPGA and oscilloscopes with concrete examples if retaining them.
items.because: Neither is demonstrated in the experience bullets.

items.says: Make “firmware” more specific.
items.because: It is broader than the other listed methods.

items.says: Prioritize methods relevant to the target roles and show where you applied them.
